newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi official stabbed on street - Japan police.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi official stabbed on street - Japan police.

text.p: An executive in charge of customer complaints at Japan's scandal-hit Yamaichi Securities was stabbed to death on a Tokyo street on Thursday night while returning home from work, a police spokesman reported.
The spokesman identified the official as Koichiro Tarutani, 57, who handled complaints from investors about share transactions made for them by the company.

"Tarutani was stabbed at about 8.20 p.m. (1120 GMT) about 10 minutes away from his home," the spokesman told Reuters. He said no arrests had been made and no motive for the stabbing was evident so far.
Yamaichi on Monday announced the resignation of its chairman, president and five vice-presidents over the firm's suspected payoffs to a racketeer.

The firm, the smallest of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, is suspected of making 79 million yen ($681,000) in illegal payoffs to Ryuichi Koike, the corporate racketeer at the heart of a financial scandal which has also ensnared giant brokerage Nomura Securities and Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB).
More than a dozen people, including top executives from Nomura and DKB, have been arrested in the affair.
